readingInstruction: Read Jeremiah 49:1-51:64. This is another survey day, with oracles against Ammon, Edom, Damascus, Elam, and above all, Babylon. Read the Babylon oracle for its main theme: the empire that destroyed Jerusalem will itself be destroyed.
settingTheScene: The long section of oracles ends with Babylon. Jeremiah’s message to the exiles is that Babylon, God’s instrument, will be punished for its own pride and cruelty. In 51:59-64, Jeremiah sends a scroll with Seraiah, a Judean official, who is to read the oracle in Babylon and then tie a stone to it and throw it into the Euphrates. Babylon fell in 539 BC, though not as dramatically as the prophecies suggest. The final fall is a symbol still awaited.
observation: “The pride of your heart has deceived you, you who live in the clefts of the rock” (49:16).
“I have heard a message from the LORD, and an envoy has been sent among the nations” (49:14).
“Declare among the nations and proclaim… Babylon is taken, Bel is put to shame, Merodach is dismayed” (50:2).
“In those days and in that time, declares the LORD, the people of Israel and the people of Judah shall come together, weeping as they come” (50:4).
“They shall ask the way to Zion, with faces turned toward it, saying, Come, let us join ourselves to the LORD in an everlasting covenant” (50:5).
“Their Redeemer is strong; the LORD of hosts is his name” (50:34).
“Babylon was a golden cup in the LORD’s hand, making all the earth drunken” (51:7).
“Flee from the midst of Babylon; let every one save his life!” (51:6).
interpretation:
The oracles against the nations in chapter 49 follow familiar notes. Edom’s pride in its mountain strongholds will not save it. “Though you make your nest as high as the eagle’s, from there I will bring you down.” Damascus and Hazor and Elam will also fall.

Chapters 50 and 51 are a long poem on Babylon. The great empire that carried God’s people into exile is now the target. The reason is stated: Babylon sinned against the LORD, the Holy One of Israel. It exulted in its destruction of his heritage. Its gods, Bel and Merodach, will be put to shame. God uses a nation from the north, the Medes and Persians, to do it. Babylon will become a desolation.

But the poem is also about Israel. In the middle of the destruction, there is a promise for God’s people: they will come together, weeping, and seek the way to Zion. “Come, let us join ourselves to the LORD in an everlasting covenant that will never be forgotten.” This is the language of the new covenant. The prophet says that their sins will be sought for and not found: “For I will pardon those whom I leave as a remnant.” The people are called to leave Babylon. “Flee from the midst of Babylon… Be not cut off in her punishment.”

The image of Babylon as a golden cup in the LORD’s hand shows God’s control. The empire was an instrument, and when it has done its work, it is broken. The scroll sunk in the Euphrates ends the prophecy with an act of faith: “Thus shall Babylon sink, to rise no more.” The last line of the section is simple: “Thus far are the words of Jeremiah.”

In Scripture, Babylon is more than a city. It becomes the symbol of the world system in opposition to God. Revelation echoes these chapters in its portrayal of the fall of Babylon the great.
connection: Revelation 18:4 says, “Come out of her, my people, lest you take part in her sins,” echoing Jeremiah 51:45. Revelation 14:8 and 18:2 declare “Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great.” Revelation 18:21 describes a millstone thrown into the sea, like Jeremiah’s scroll. Hebrews 8:8-12 confirms the “everlasting covenant” in Christ. 2 Corinthians 6:17 calls us to come out and be separate.
application:
Ask what “Babylon” looks like in your context: a system or value that opposes God. How are you called to live as a faithful exile?

Join in the prayer of Jeremiah 50:5: “Come, let us join ourselves to the LORD in an everlasting covenant.”

Remember that no empire lasts forever. Place your hope in the kingdom of God.
prayerPrompts: Thank God that he is the Redeemer who judges proud powers.
Ask him to help you come out of whatever he calls you to leave.
Pray for his people living among empires.
